analyst_view.overall: Early view: Porto have won all 11 league games (27-5) under Francesco Farioli and lead third-placed Sporting by 9 points, so this is the biggest test of their streak. Sporting have just changed coach, with Paulo Fonseca replacing Rui Borges and winning his debut 1-0 against Moreirense. Both play in the Champions League that week: Porto at Feyenoord on Tuesday 24 November, Sporting at home to Manchester United on Wednesday 25, so Sporting have a day less to recover.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Porto have conceded only 5 times in 11 games and their streak is built on control, while Fonseca has had little time to change Sporting, whose first game under him was a hard-earned 1-0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Porto will likely have more of the ball at home, and Sporting under Fonseca are reported to be focused on keeping possession, so neither side should sit very deep. I see no strong reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.9 cards, already a high figure that reflects how heated this fixture usually is. The referee has not been named yet, and that will matter more than anything else here. I keep to the site's figure for now.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots. I lean lower: both teams come off Champions League nights, Sporting with only three days' rest, and a 9-point gap makes Porto comfortable with a controlled game. Gabriel Mec's thigh injury and Bednarek's eye problem are worth checking after the break.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Porto allow very few clear chances and Sporting are still adapting to a new coach. I expect a tighter count of efforts that actually test the goalkeepers.
